source: Heinrich Werner, Die Jenissej-Sprachen des 18. Jahrhunderts (2005)
scope: Arin chapter; primary scan checked at printed pp. 149-155

findings.claim: Werner explicitly says not all persons are attested and the full predicative personal-suffix system can only be reconstructed by analogy with other Yeniseian languages.
Werner's reconstructed table gives 1PL -taŋ/*-toŋ, 2PL *-kaŋ/*-koŋ, 3PL animate -aŋ/-iaŋ, and 3PL inanimate -a.
On the same page the verbal form at'aŋ-taŋ is glossed 'wir stehen' = 'we stand', i.e. first-person plural.

Werner introduces the Arin 'stand' forms as Ganz eigentümlich ('quite peculiar'). The paradigm gives the same surface predicate ending -taŋ for 1PL and 3PL; the 3PL line carries a tentative derivational note (< -aŋ ?).
The Arin lexicon entry for 'stand' independently repeats source-labelled 1PL, 2PL and 3PL forms; 1PL and 3PL again share the same surface predicate.

model_effect.retain: A 3PL Arin surface form ending in -taŋ is independently attested, so formal compatibility with the Ji couplet is real.
model_effect.downgrade: Werner 2005 does not support treating -taŋ as a clean unique 3PL diagnostic. In his generalized reconstruction -taŋ is 1PL, while animate 3PL is -aŋ/-iaŋ, and the 'stand' paradigm is explicitly peculiar and syncretic between 1PL and 3PL.
model_effect.recommended_scoring: Replace +2 Arin-specific 3PL diagnostic with +1 surface compatibility and -1 non-diagnostic/syncretism challenge (net 0 for this subclaim).
